questions.stem:
Okoye Stores uses component X at the following rates: maximum usage 450 units per week, average usage 300 units per week, minimum usage 150 units per week. The lead time is 3 to 5 weeks (average 4 weeks). The reorder quantity is 2,400 units.
(a) Calculate (i) the reorder level; (ii) the minimum stock level; (iii) the maximum stock level. [12 marks]
(b) Explain two dangers of holding too much stock and two dangers of holding too little stock. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 450 x 5
2 marks: reorder level = 2,250 units
2 marks: minimum = reorder level - (average usage x average lead time) = 2,250 - 1,200
2 marks: minimum level = 1,050 units
2 marks: maximum = reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage x minimum lead time) = 2,250 + 2,400 - 450
2 marks: maximum level = 4,200 units
2 marks: overstocking ties up capital
2 marks: overstocking increases storage costs, deterioration, theft or obsolescence
2 marks: understocking causes stock-outs and lost sales
2 marks: understocking halts production / loses customer goodwill / leads to costly emergency orders
questions.explanation: Reorder level = 450 x 5 = 2,250. Minimum = 2,250 - (300 x 4) = 1,050. Maximum = 2,250 + 2,400 - (150 x 3) = 4,200 units. Too much stock ties up capital and raises storage, spoilage and theft costs; too little causes stock-outs, lost sales and goodwill, and emergency buying.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of stock control. [3 marks]
(b) State four reasons for stock control in a store. [8 marks]
(c) Describe the use of each of the following stock records: (i) bin card; (ii) store requisition form; (iii) delivery note. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the system of ensuring that the right quantity and quality of stock is available at the right time at minimum cost
2 marks: to avoid overstocking and tying up capital
2 marks: to avoid stock-outs and production stoppages
2 marks: to prevent theft, waste and deterioration
2 marks: to provide information for accounts and decision making / to know when to reorder
3 marks: bin card: kept with each item to record receipts, issues and balance in quantities
3 marks: store requisition form: written request from a department authorising issue of materials from the store
3 marks: delivery note: accompanies goods from the supplier, checked and signed on receipt
questions.explanation: Stock control keeps the right quantity and quality of stock at minimum cost. It avoids overstocking and stock-outs, reduces theft and waste, signals reorder points and supports accounting. Bin cards record quantities received and issued; requisitions authorise issues; delivery notes accompany and confirm deliveries.

questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the sale of goods in small quantities to final consumers
2 marks: sells in small quantities convenient for consumers
2 marks: stocks a variety of goods for choice
2 marks: locates near consumers for convenience
2 marks: gives credit and after-sales services
2 marks: gives advice and information on products

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following: (i) patent; (ii) copyright; (iii) trade mark. [9 marks]
(b) State the roles of each of the following government regulatory agencies: (i) NAFDAC; (ii) SON; (iii) NDLEA. [9 marks]
(c) State one reason why a store manager should know these regulations. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: patent: exclusive right granted to an inventor to make, use and sell an invention for a period
3 marks: copyright: exclusive right of an author or creator to reproduce literary, artistic or musical works
3 marks: trade mark: registered sign, name or symbol distinguishing a firm's goods from others
3 marks: NAFDAC regulates manufacture, import, sale and advertisement of food, drugs, cosmetics and chemicals
3 marks: SON sets and enforces product quality standards
3 marks: NDLEA controls and prevents trafficking and abuse of illicit drugs
2 marks: to avoid stocking fake, substandard or banned products and so avoid sanctions and protect customers
questions.explanation: Patents protect inventions; copyright protects creative works; trade marks identify a firm's goods. NAFDAC regulates food, drugs and cosmetics; SON enforces standards; NDLEA fights illicit drugs. Knowing these avoids stocking fake or banned goods and legal penalties.

questions.stem:
The petty cashier of Ade Stores operates an imprest of N25,000. During the first week of March the following payments were made: transport N3,200; stationery N4,750; cleaning N2,500; postage N1,800; refreshment for visitors N3,150; transport N1,600.
(a) Explain the imprest system. [4 marks]
(b) Calculate (i) the total expenditure for the week; (ii) the balance in hand; (iii) the amount to be reimbursed. [6 marks]
(c) Calculate the total of the transport column if the petty cash book is analysed. [2 marks]
(d) State four advantages of the imprest system. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: a fixed float is given to the petty cashier and at the end of the period the amount spent is reimbursed to restore the float
2 marks: total expenditure = N17,000
2 marks: balance in hand = 25,000 - 17,000 = N8,000
2 marks: reimbursement = N17,000
2 marks: transport = 3,200 + 1,600 = N4,800
2 marks: relieves the main cashier of small payments
2 marks: easy control because spending is checked at each reimbursement
2 marks: limits fraud since the float is small
2 marks: provides training for junior staff / analysis of expenses
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system the petty cashier holds a fixed float, and expenditure is reimbursed at intervals. Total spent = 3,200 + 4,750 + 2,500 + 1,800 + 3,150 + 1,600 = 17,000; balance 8,000; reimbursement 17,000. Transport = 4,800. Advantages: frees the chief cashier, easy control, limited risk of fraud, training and expense analysis.

questions.stem:
(a) Define tax. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four types of taxes that affect a store business in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) A store sells goods worth N800,000 (excluding VAT). Calculate the VAT charged at the rate of 7.5%. [4 marks]
(d) State three importance of taxation to the government. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a compulsory levy imposed by government on individuals and businesses
2 marks: company/personal income tax on profits or income
2 marks: value added tax on goods and services sold
2 marks: import duties on goods brought into the country
2 marks: excise duties on locally manufactured goods
2 marks: 7.5% x 800,000 shown
2 marks: VAT = N60,000
2 marks: source of revenue for government expenditure
2 marks: redistribution of income
2 marks: regulation of the economy / discouraging harmful goods / protecting local industries
questions.explanation: Tax is a compulsory levy. Stores face income tax, VAT, import duties and excise duties. VAT = 7.5% x 800,000 = N60,000. Taxes raise revenue, redistribute income, regulate the economy and protect local industries.
